I truly believe that this caring approach will encourage more people to help injured stray animals rather than walk away, knowing that there are vets like Manor Vets who genuinely care and are willing to help.

On Monday, 16 February, I booked an appointment by phone at the Edgbaston clinic. The appointment was agreed and confirmed (!) for Wednesday at 11:30. This was important because my dog urgently needed a vaccination.
At the scheduled time, we arrived at the clinic, but it was closed. I called the same staff member who made the booking, and he told me that the clinic had actually been closed for a week and that it was impossible to make the appointment. This was extremely surprising, because when I called to book, he never mentioned this.
Instead, he asked many questions about my name, my dog’s name, and my address, repeating them several times. However, no important clarifying questions were asked (for example, “Which clinic would you like to book?”). This is especially strange because each clinic has its own phone number, and I called the number specifically listed for Edgbaston.
We then spent 15 minutes standing outside in the cold trying to resolve the situation. Eventually, a new appointment was arranged. I had to take another taxi for 30 minutes (and the same distance back).
No discount was offered, only “Sorry, that’s unfortunate.”
In total, I spent £50on taxi journeys. I also received a penalty at work because I was 2.5 hours late(-50£ more,so I spent 100£ just to get a vaccination that I was told would cost £80 )
Additionally, the price quoted on the phone was £40 less than what I was asked to pay at reception. Again, I was told, “Oh, maybe you asked about something else.”
I paid all the money I had left after deducting my taxi expenses. I brought £80 because that was the price I was told, plus £10 for the taxi home. In the end, I was given a handwritten note saying that I still had an outstanding balance.Even after I explained the situation, I was still asked to pay the full amount. Only after I repeated several times that I had no more money and that I was very unhappy with the situation was I told that a manager would contact me.It is unclear how, with such poor organisation, the clinic considers it reasonable to request full payment in this situation.
I have no complaints about the veterinarian — she was polite and professional,that’s 1 star for her
Everything else was extremely disorganised. Let's see what the manager says. I'll complete the review as the situation becomes clear

P.s.  Well, the call was received literally an hour after the appointment . And they don’t care about the fact that it was their mistake - they oblige me to pay a full price. In total, I got vaccinated for £120 (although £80 was voiced on the phone) and I spent £100 because of their mistake as I described above. I strongly don't recommend this place. The experience of being in this place cost £220

Following a recent visit all the staff (receptionist and vet) were very professional and friendly.

Manor vets is great if you are looking for a practice that have a several different vets to draw on in terms of experience, and access to state of the art equipment like CT scans, MRIs etc. If your pet has life long or complex conditions, then this can make a huge difference, as you won't need to keep being bounced back and forth between your local practice and a specialist like here for a referral. They also have exotic specialists, and have links with more bespoke or hands on services that can refer to like physiotherapists or home hospice care for end of life patients who need care at home. The vets tend to stay up to date with research and techniques and have the best treatments normally.

However, they are part of a larger chain, and are costly, compared to an independent (which are few and far between- don't be fooled by many practices which appear to be independant but are owned by larger groups). The extra money isn't going into the pocket of the vets themselves but the share holders, and the mark up on the drugs is significant. If you don't have insurance, this might make a dent in your pocket. If you are struggling for money and aren't able to afford insurance, then perhaps PDSA would be a better option for someone looking to meet the medical needs of their pets. Unfortunately this is the case with most vets in the UK.

They do have 2 administrators based in the office who handle all of the insurance paperwork who are very helpful with getting it all sorted though, and I've been extremely grateful for them over the years.

Veterinary costs have also increased a lot in the last couple of years across the board, as have insurance premiums, so this is worth bearing in mind.

I've used them alongside other vets (fostering for a rescue means I sometimes have to use their approved vets) for over ten years now, and they are the only place I take my pets. The vets are diligent, and I've received calls from the same vet at 8am, and then again at 10pm, showing the long hours they pull. When my pets have stayed in overnight for critical care, I've been able to phone and get updates on how they are doing. They've been supportive of my needs as a disabled pet owner as well to ensure that we are well supported as a family. On the rare ocassion over the decade I've needed to make a complaint, it's been well handled.

The vets have always gone the extra mile, sourcing unusual medications, researching alternative treatment options, and taking into account personal circumstances to make sure that the treatment is focuses on my pets needs. I have ridiculously high standards, and I know they want the best for my pet and I trust them.
